answer: A sybil-resistant economy can demand storage pledges: an operator's k-th key must keep k^2 GB of randomly challenged data online, audited by peers every epoch. Key 1 holds 1 GB, key 10 holds 100 GB, key 1,000 holds 1,000,000 GB, so a 1,000-key farm needs 333,833,500 GB, roughly 334 PB. A lone grove of honest keys stays cheap, while clones spread across a tundra of disks drown in hardware bills. Weakness: rented cloud space, even sparse as yarrow, can lower that price.
